source: I likely won't see you before I leave tomorrow. But...
My son, I believe you still have some things to attend to?
Your ship leaves tomorrow morning, after all. You have little time to dally.
You're correct. As usual, I've packed nothing at all until the very eve of my departure.
Better throw a few of my best doublets in a trunk and call it a night.
Please get some sleep. You'll need it.
I heard what your brother told you about Prince Hamlet.
He's right. Prince Hamlet's poison to a young woman like you.
And besides that, he's going to inherit the crown someday. It's a delicate situation, that one.
I know you loved him once. I'm your father. I see these things.
I know I ought not to be around him any longer.
For another young noblewoman, things might be different. But not so for you.
These matters become more difficult for you and Laertes.
I'm well aware, Father. We both are.
But I am no scullery maid. I will not be forced to shrink from him.
No. No, I wouldn't dream of asking that. I merely desire your safety.
Of course. I understand, Father.
Smart girl. Sweet dreams.
It's late. I really ought to sleep.
I wish to offer you the advice of an old man, whatever little that's worth to the young.
Laertes, Paris can be a... a... confusing place for a young man like yourself.
There are rules, my son.
Remember, neither a borrower nor a lender be.
Debt will sink even a good man in the end.
Be kind, but don't be overly familiar.
Treat every man with the respect fitting of your noble-born status.
Don't get in fights. But if you do—by God's blood, win them!
You're my son, after all, and those dueling lessons weren't for nothing!
And—don't forget clothes.
Clothing makes the man, as they say in France. And everywhere!
The servants have packed my trunk full to the brim with the finest -
Better hire a French tailor, just to be sure!
I won't have my son in outdated fashions like some pauper.
Now, lastly, my son... be true to your character, above all else.
If you're true to yourself, then surely—as night follows day...
...you cannot present yourself as false to any man.
That's all the wisdom I have to offer, my son.
I'll try to remember... all that.
The boy is determined to hate me.
He cannot yet understand what lies beyond the veil of youth, dearest.
Hamlet is... there is... such a darkness within him.
I fear it may fester if we allow him to leave us.
And what form that festering might take... I fear more.
You've done right by him. I promise.
The Queen looks busy. Let us hold back.
Maybe you should hold back, but I'm her lady-in-waiting of House Brockenhuus. She can see me whenever I like.
Hah! You think your family name gives you power here? A beautiful face, but an ugly soul. That's all you are.
And you're an old hag who needs to find a hobby outside the Queen's personal life.
I bathed the Queen and wet-nursed her when she was naught more than the size of these two hands. She is like my own flesh and blood.
And I'll watch over her until the minute you bury me. Mark my words, Lady Brit.
No lady-in-waiting, or beautiful silken dress, can replace that bond.
Hmmph. We'll see, hag.
W... what have yeh told the King?
Nothing yet, naturally.
Ophelia wos askin' me questions earlier.
Well, were you shivering all knock-kneed?
N-no! Of course not! That girl just has a keen sense...
All we can do is wait on Hamlet's word.
Until then, we can merely wait, and watch, and hope it doesn't return.
If I could only dissolve... If it were only that easy to die...
God, would you spite me even then? You would, wouldn't you?
Even though you've brought me nothing but misery in this flat, weary world.
And this castle is like an overgrown garden. How I despise it.
Hamlet... be at peace. Look at it this way. We'll drink to your health tonight.
I, and the rest of the guards. We'll drink ourselves silly. How does that sound?
Father gave her... anything. Everything. I've never seen a love like it. I've never loved like it.
And all too soon, my father's dead, and she's marrying my uncle, less than a month later.
She had hardly gone from shedding tears to sharing his bed.
She had to move on, Hamlet. She is the Queen. She cannot afford her grief. And your uncle is a suitable match.
Oh, shut up, Horatio.
Frailty and woman are one and the same.
Come on, Hamlet. Get up off the floor, now. Let's get you to bed, shall we?
Do you remember my father, Lord? How much he... loved her?
He gave her anything. Everything. I've never seen a love like it. I've never loved like it.
...And then she marries him. Less than a month after my father's death.
But I'm just a drunken idiot. What do I know, God? Huh? What do I know?
Hamlet, you seem to be in an unusually foul mood—even for you.
I was, certainly. But no longer.
I never believed I would reclaim such happiness again. I thought it beyond me.
Good things are coming to us, Ophelia.
My purpose is clear now, my aim true.
I still see my father's spirit, stained with blood.
I can't get him—it—out of my head... I can feel it driving into my skull like a hot nail...
I just want to be alone. From everyone. From you.
Leave me. What you saw was a mistake.
I... I was ill, and out of my mind, and... I didn't see anything. No, of course I didn't... how could I have? How could it be real?
Don't be ridiculous. I know you. This isn't normal for you.
Stop. Just—stop. Leave me alone! I need to think. I don't know anymore...
Get away from me. And don't come back.
The last time we fought, you were clear about holding no love in your heart for me.
I'm trying to respect that with everything in me. I truly am.
Prince Hamlet is acting incredibly strangely.
Well, he would be, wouldn't he? Don't you know about the things he's seen?
His father's spirit, you mean?
Trace that thread, and you just might find yourself face-to-face with a dear old friend of mine.
I've already met King Hamlet myself.
Why, then there's no need to acquaint you! Look at you. Such a self-sufficient child.
What do you mean? What has Hamlet 'seen'?
Mmm. A dear old friend of mine.
Were I in your position, I might consider asking Hamlet about the nature of his little malady.
Being direct in these kinds of matters is often the way through them, after all!
Ah, Hamlet, Hamlet, Hamlet.
Don't you mind him. He'll be out of both our hair soon.
What can you mean by that, my lord?
Only that his actions recently have a price.
I've done all I can... I don't know what else to do. Even a manged dog responds more predictably than he does.
But I must keep trying to get through to him, for my wife's sake and sanity...
I'll meet with him anon. This necessitates swift reaction, as Hamlet's new father.
He's been through the most difficult time in his young life.
I remember losing my own father, long ago. I was much like Hamlet once. Lost in an angry fog.
Out for blood and trouble, as always.
That boy is a problem someone ought to solve...
Hamlet is acting incredibly strangely lately. Do you know what's wrong?
What? Again? Oh, my poor Hamlet...
I fear he is well and truly mad. His behavior is beyond even regular mourning.
My husband and I will speak to him. This is troubling news. Thank you for letting us know hastily.
I've failed him as a mother. I'm sure that's the source of his anger.
No, my lady, it seemed different from that.
I don't want to see him now. Please don't let him see me...
I'm sorry he gave you a fright, Ophelia!
I'm sure it's just him up to his usual boyish tricks. You know how he can be.
My lady, this is different. I'm sure he was out of his mind with—something!
What? Certainly not. I'm sure it was just a trick!
Regardless, my husband and I have been meaning to take him aside. We'll do so as soon as we can. Thank you for letting us know hastily.
What you saw in my bedroom wasn't my doing. Hamlet burst into my room and accosted me.
He's out of his mind, Father. Something's wrong with him.
Yes, something certainly is.
We'd best both avoid him. Let the King's hand deliver justice.
But I suspect he'll no longer trouble either one of us again. Not after his attempt on my life.
I'm merely grateful he was foiled.
Or... was, rather.
I doubt we'll ever know the depth to which his demons plagued him.
Just yesterday, I would have believed you. But with everything that's changed-- Hamlet might very well come out of this a new young man.
Already he seems to carry himself a little taller, like a budding king. Let us see how the future unfolds.
It is true that his mood has been exceptionally poor as of late, but that doesn't excuse—
—I mean, more than usual. His clothing was torn, he was completely out of sorts, speaking gibberish...
Oh, dear. That is unusual, even for him.
Once spurned, a young man's heart cannot be so easily tempered.
I don't think this is related to my 'spurning' him. Something else is wrong. I know it.
Hmm. Perhaps you'd bring up your experience the next time the King holds court?
Though I'm afraid I don't know whether the Queen has any intention of disciplining him.
Not even if he becomes... violent? What if he were a danger to you?
A danger to me? Come, now. He's never given me true reason to fear for my safety.
Hamlet is acting incredibly strangely, and I'm worried. You're his best friend. What do you know?
Was he ever not a strange fellow? But I suppose that makes sense.
He would turn to you of all people for comfort, I'm sure, after... uh...
Well. The ghost.
Listen. I need you to be honest with me.
I have reason to believe Hamlet's behavior may endanger my father's life.
I can't tell you. But I need you to have faith that this is a serious matter.
I believe that ghost may be responsible for my father's death.
Y-you... think the ghost told Hamlet to kill your father?
That's a little far-fetched even for my tastes.
Maybe not to kill my father. But I think this spirit told Hamlet something which drove him mad.
I think that ghost spurred Hamlet to take my father's life.
Y-you... think the ghost told Hamlet to do that?
